cards.explanation: The answer is: so they know they have eternal life. The writer says, "I have written these things to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, so that you may know that you have eternal life." (1 John 5:13) He doesn't want his readers guessing or crossing their fingers, friends. He wants them to KNOW.

The answer is: according to His will. "If we ask anything according to His will, He hears us." (1 John 5:14) Notice he says anything, and he says He hears. The key is asking in line with what God wants, friends.

The answer is False. The text says, "And if we know that He hears us in whatever we ask, we know that we already possess what we have asked of Him." (1 John 5:15) So believers can be sure, not stuck wondering. Lots of us check the oven ten times, friends, but here the writer says we know.

The answer is: ask God for him. The writer says he "…should ask God, who will give life to those who commit this kind of sin." (1 John 5:16) So he asks God for his brother, and God is the One who gives life. Asking is the action the verse names, friends.

The answer is False. The writer says, "There is a sin that leads to death; I am not saying he should ask regarding that sin." (1 John 5:16) He tells believers to ask for the sin not leading to death, and he doesn't say to ask about this one, friends. The text doesn't tell us more than that.

The word is protects. "…the One who was born of God protects him, and the evil one cannot touch him." (1 John 5:18) Anyone born of God has someone watching over him, friends. That's a better deal than my old junk drawer, where the only protection was a rubber band.

The answer is True. The writer says, "…the One who was born of God protects him, and the evil one cannot touch him." (1 John 5:18) The protection and the "cannot touch" come together, friends. Read it twice, it's good.

The answer is: the power of the evil one. The writer says, "…the whole world is under the power of the evil one." (1 John 5:19) He sets that next to "…we are of God…" Two very different places to stand, friends.

The word is understanding. The writer says the Son of God "…has given us understanding, so that we may know Him who is true…" (1 John 5:20) Understanding is what He gave, and it leads to knowing Him, friends. That's a gift better than any fresh batch.
The answer is False. The writer says, "…we are in Him who is true—in His Son Jesus Christ." (1 John 5:20) Believers aren't far away, friends. They are in Him. That's about as close as it gets.

The answer is: idols. The last line of the letter says, "Little children, keep yourselves from idols." (1 John 5:21) After all that talk about the true God, he ends with a warning to stay away from idols, friends. Short and strong.
